prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Fluid Mechanics Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Mechanical Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability of oral expression.
Ability of written expression.
Ability to learn and work autonomously.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Know the main characteristics and behavior of hydraulic machines.
Describe the basic operation of hydraulic turbomachines: pumps and turbines.
Apply the general equations of fluid mechanics to the study of hydraulic installations equipped with turbomachines.
Know how to use dimensional analysis techniques and the concept of physical similarity in the field of turbomachinery.
Work with and extract information from the characteristic curves of hydraulic turbomachines.
Know the main characteristics and behavior of different pump couplings to the network.
Carry out relevant studies and understand the main phenomena associated with excessive depressions and overpressures in hydraulic installations and machines: cavitation and water hammer.
Know the fundamentals of hydraulic circuits and distribution systems.
Know the fundamentals of reverse osmosis water desalination plants.
Autonomous learning.
Teamwork.
Ability to pose and solve problems within the scope of the subject.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1.- Introduction to hydraulic machines
Introduction and historical review. Definition. Classification. General aspects.
Topic 2.- Hydraulic Turbomachines: Pumps and Turbines
Classification. Constituent elements. Fundamental equation. Characteristic installations.
Topic 3.- Similarity in hydraulic turbomachines
Introduction. Pump similarity laws. Turbine similarity laws. Specific speed.
Topic 4.- Characteristic Curves of hydraulic turbomachines
Elementary test and complete test of a pump. Characteristic Curves of pumps. Characteristic Curves of turbines.
Topic 5.- Cavitation in hydraulic installations and machines
Description and study of the phenomenon. Cavitation control.
Topic 6.- Coupling of pumps to the network.
Introduction. Parallel coupling of pumps. Series coupling of pumps.
Topic 7.- Water hammer in hydraulic installations and machines
Description and study of the phenomenon. Main control measures for water hammer.
Topic 8.- Fundamentals of hydraulic circuits and distribution systems
Introduction. Supply with two or more tanks. Fundamentals of distribution networks.
Topic 9.- Fundamentals of reverse osmosis water desalination plants
Desalination procedures. Fundamentals of reverse osmosis desalination plant.
Practice 1.- Characterization of head losses in hydraulic installations (laboratory practice)
Practice 2.- Study and characterization of centrifugal pump (laboratory practice)
Practice 3.- Analysis of hydraulic distribution system using software (Epanet)
Practice 4.- Field practice. Reverse osmosis desalination
Seminar.- Wind turbine test bench
teaching_methods: Problem-solving sessions for better understanding and practical application
Exposition and development of theoretical content during problem-solving
Student-led problem posing and development with professor guidance
Laboratory practices with guided work for small groups
Technical visit (field practice) to a hydraulic installation

assessment_methods.method: Written exam on all theoretical and practical contents of Part I (Continuous Assessment)
Reports corresponding to laboratory practices 1, 2 and 3 (the last one in English) (Continuous Assessment)
Written exam on all theoretical and practical contents of Part II (Continuous Assessment)
Exam covering all theoretical and practical contents of the subject (Single Assessment)
Reports corresponding to laboratory practices 1, 2 and 3 (the last one in English) (Single Assessment)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 4 is required in the Part I exam (EvC1), and 4.5 in the Part II exam (EvC3) and the practice reports (EvC2). If these minimums are not met, the final grade is a fail, taking the lowest quantitative grade obtained in EvC1, EvC2, or EvC3. Attendance to all practical sessions is mandatory for EvC2. The continuous assessment mode does not apply to the second call or successive calls. For single assessment, a minimum grade of 4.5 is required in both the final exam (Ev1) and the practice reports (Ev2). Students who did not attend laboratory sessions or did not pass them during the semester must take a practical lab exam to obtain a passing grade for the practical component.
